_comment: THE PRODUCTION RETRAIN. Train on every supervised cell, stop at a fixed epoch, ship the
result. Two knobs, and they must move TOGETHER -- see the trap at the bottom.
ESK_DESK_CONFIG=config/overlays/production.json STAGES=desk bash scripts/tacc/submit_encoder.sh
ESK_DESK_CONFIG=config/overlays/production.json STAGES=cube bash scripts/tacc/submit_encoder.sh
It lives in an overlay rather than the base so the committed default stays the HOLDOUT
config every sweep and every validation run uses. Putting holdout_frac=0 in the base would
silently hand the next sweep a configuration that cannot select an epoch or report a score.
WHY 200. desk_hp stage 1 under --smooth 11 puts base's robust optimum at epoch 170. The raw
argmin says 107 and the separate full-length run in 9aa07ff said 117, but kernel_val swings
~2x between adjacent epochs at high LR, so a raw argmin is a single lucky evaluation rather
than a property of the model -- smoothing moves base by 63 epochs. 200 is 1.18x of 170, a
modest allowance for the training data this pass gains by dropping the holdout and its
buffer ring, and it sits inside the range of complete runs (122-256 smoothed) rather than
beyond it.
It is NOT read off a fit, and it should have been. analyze.py --stage 2 exists to regress
best epoch on log training cell-years and extrapolate to the production data amount, but
all 25 desk_hp runs sit in one cell (t0_f100) -- the train_frac axis was never run -- so
there is no trajectory. 170 is therefore a LOWER BOUND measured at a smaller data amount,
and 200 is a judgement above it, not a measurement. Running desk.trend.train_frac over
f70/f85/f95 would replace the judgement with a fit.
WHY base RATHER THAN hl4. hl4 leads the smoothed ranking by 3.8% and is best on k@24 (the
column that ships), but the seed-to-seed spread is 6.6% sd / 15.6% full range, measured
from hl4's OWN three replicates. A 3.8% margin inside a 6.6% floor is not a result. Settling
it is ~6-10 runs of hl4 and base at additional seeds and no new code; until then base is the
configuration with the most evidence behind it, not the better one.
LATENT WIDTH IS UNCHANGED at 64, and the age model's positional truncation to 24 stays. The
eigenbasis table reports base's best rank as 8 with rank 64 costing +2.5% -- but rank 24,
which is what model_inputs actually keeps, costs only +0.5%. The penalty the pipeline pays
is already near zero, and narrowing would move AWAY from bestR. Refitting the basis at 32
is separately closed: ESK's own rank curve improves 11x from r8 to r64 out of sample, so the
tail is real signal and a low per-run bestR is the encoder failing to predict it, not a
basis that is too wide. (Those diagnostics were measured at epoch 110, not 170; the rank
profile at 200 is unmeasured.)
THE TRAP. stop_at_epoch and holdout_frac must be set together. With holdout_frac=0 there is
no validation set, so nothing can select an epoch -- desk_training keeps the FINAL weights
and takes its stopping point from stop_at_epoch alone. Leave stop_at_epoch null here and the
run trains all 500 epochs and ships the over-trained state, which 9aa07ff measured as
actively worse (the held-out kernel DEGRADES past the optimum, it does not plateau). Nothing
catches that combination.
And stop_at_epoch halts the loop WITHOUT shortening the LR schedule: _warmup_cosine is
parameterised on the epochs BUDGET, so lowering `epochs` to 200 instead would change the
learning rate at every preceding step and train a different model rather than the same one
stopped earlier. epochs stays 500.
This run has no measured skill of its own, by design. Its evidence is the desk_hp sweep and
the desk_tempho_* holdout runs, all on the same encoder/esk_balanced/spacetime basis.
